newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria's IG Metall seeks five percent pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria's IG Metall seeks five percent pay rise.

text.p: The Bavarian branch of Germany's largest trade union, IG Metall, said on Wednesday it would go into the next round of pay talks seeking a five percent increase in wages and salaries.

The metal and engineering union said it wanted to make sure that any wage agreements contained policies to secure jobs, such as measures which allow overtime hours to be remunerated as time-in-lieu and part-time work for older employees.

Werner Neugebauer, head of IG Metall in Bavaria, said fighting unemployment was the union's first priority, adding that the union's demands on holiday pay and Christmas pay, rejected by employers, must be reinstated.

Bavarian IG Metall cancelled existing wage agreements with effect from January 31 and has warned firms the union is prepared to strike over the issue of sick pay. A new law which came into force in October allows employers to reduce sick pay by 20 percent.
The union said that it can strike from the start of February if agreement is not reached on the controversial issue.
